questions.question: Which record sets the current per-frame budget for Skiff's 40 Hz mode?
traps: Four Constraints share the title "Frame budget". The render Effort's live one covers Meridian at 16.6 ms.
The render Effort holds a retracted "Frame budget" with the 25 ms Skiff figure; retracted records are not current.

questions.question: Across every Effort, how many live Constraints are titled "Frame budget"?
traps: Counting superseded or retracted versions gives 7.
Reading one Effort gives 1.

questions.question: Across every Effort, how many retracted records are titled exactly "Frame budget"?
traps: Browse reads omit retracted records, so a reader using only `records` finds none.

questions.question: The co-op rollback prototype was abandoned because of a Decision made in a different Effort. Which Decision?

where.title: Run the tide simulation in 32.32 fixed point

checks.includes: Run the tide simulation in 32.32 fixed point

traps: The netcode Effort is abandoned, so `proof list` with its default status hides it.
The answer is named only by title in prose; no edge links the two Efforts.

questions.question: Who wrote the Decision that the netcode Effort cites as the reason it abandoned rollback?
traps: Sofia Marchetti wrote the abandonment Decision, not the Decision it cites.

questions.question: Rollback had to re-run the tides every frame on Skiff. Roughly what share of the Skiff 40 Hz frame budget did that cost?

includes: a fifth of the 25 ms frame

traps: Using the 33.3 ms 30 Hz frame gives about 14 percent.
Using the render Effort's 16.6 ms Frame budget gives about 29 percent.

questions.question: The streaming pool's last size cut names a Skiff memory limit from another Effort as its reason. What is that Skiff limit today?
traps: Both versions of "Skiff memory budget" share a title; the 9 GB one is superseded.
The streaming pool's own figure, 1.6 GB, is not the Skiff limit.

questions.question: What Skiff memory budget was in force when the world Effort first set the streaming pool budget?
traps: The first streaming pool budget dates from September 2025; the first Skiff memory budget was written in late October 2025. Answering 9 GB assumes a record that did not yet exist.

questions.question: When the world Effort cut the streaming pool to 1.6 GB, which version of the Skiff memory budget was current?
traps: The cut was made in June, four months after the 8 GB version replaced the 9 GB one in February.

questions.question: Skiff players stop hitching on their second visit to a district because of a shader cache. Which Decision created that cache?

checks.bodyIncludes: Everyone on the team calls this the shader cache

traps: The tools Effort's content-addressed shader compile cache speeds up the build farm and never reaches players.

questions.question: Does the build farm's shader compile cache ship to players on Skiff?
traps: Both caches are called "shader cache" in casual prose; only the on-device pipeline cache runs on Skiff.

questions.question: Streaming on Skiff must also work for players who install to budget microSD cards. What is the worst sustained read rate measured on those cards when full and warm?
traps: The world Effort's 190 MB/s is internal storage on retail units.
The ports Finding of 92 MB/s used new, empty cards on a cold Skiff and was invalidated.
The 61 MB/s figure sits past the browse excerpt.

questions.question: The Meridian 120 Hz mode lets Tern drop to its lowest preset. Which preset does the Skiff port run Tern at, and how many milliseconds does it save over Quality?
traps: The render Effort owns Tern, but the Skiff preset choice lives in the ports Effort.

questions.question: How many Efforts are still active?
traps: Counting every Effort gives 5; the tools Effort is completed and the netcode Effort abandoned.

questions.question: Which Efforts are no longer active, and how did each one end?
traps: `proof list` shows only active Efforts unless asked for other statuses.

questions.question: How many milliseconds per frame separate the Meridian 120 Hz mode's budget from the Skiff 40 Hz mode's budget?
traps: Using the render Effort's "Frame budget" of 16.6 ms gives 8.4 ms.
The 120 Hz budget's first version was soft and superseded; the current one is hard at 8.3 ms.

questions.question: Is the record titled exactly "Ship Tern as the only upscaler in Lantern" the Decision that the Skiff port names as its reason for using Tern?
traps: The near-identical title is a retracted duplicate; the ports Decision names "Ship Tern as Lantern's only upscaler".
